info.name: rSTAR HRMS API
info.description:
HRMS backend API.

Run the requests top to bottom. The bearer token is captured automatically:
verify-otp stores it in the {{accessToken}} variable, and every request
inherits the collection-level Bearer auth that reads it. Nothing is pasted.

Set {{baseUrl}} in the Variables tab (or pick an environment) and go.

request.description: Step 1: checks email + password, then issues an OTP.

exec: // Every endpoint answers in the same envelope - see 'Response contract'
// in the README. Asserting it here means a regression shows up on any
// request, not just the one somebody remembered to check.
pm.test('a fresh OTP was issued', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
// `data` is NOT a safe name here: the Postman sandbox predeclares it for
// the current data-file row, so `const data = ...` is a redeclaration and
// the whole script dies with a SyntaxError before a single test runs.
// The resent code REPLACES the one login issued, so the variable has to
// move with it or verify-otp will submit a code the server has forgotten.
console.warn('No OTP in response - the otp variable is now STALE. Read',
'the new code from the server log before running verify-otp.');

request.description: Issues a fresh OTP for a login already in progress, replacing the one from step 3. Only valid between login and verify-otp - once verify-otp succeeds the code is cleared and this answers 401.

request.description: Step 1 of the forgot-password flow. Matches work email + date of birth against dbo.tblEmployeeDetails (active, not soft-deleted) and emails a reset code to the work address on file. 401 when neither matches.

exec: // Every endpoint answers in the same envelope - see 'Response contract'
// in the README. Asserting it here means a regression shows up on any
// request, not just the one somebody remembered to check.
// The account this flow resets is forgotEmail. If that is also the
// account the collection logs in with, the old password just stopped
// working - carry the new one forward so a second run still gets past
console.log('loginPassword updated to match the new password.');

request.description:
Step 2 of the forgot-password flow. Exchanges the emailed code for a new password: the hash is written to dbo.EmployeeLogin, ModifiedAt is stamped and the code is cleared, so it cannot be used twice.

This really does change the password. newPassword is a fixed value, so re-running the collection sets it to the same thing and stays repeatable.
